transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hello Doctor. I guess what brought me in today is... well, I blew up at one of the younger volunteers recently. It was over something completely foolish, just a crooked tablecloth. But I really lost my temper. I don't usually talk to people that way, it's just not like me at all. So, I figured I ought to come in and see what's going on.
Have you experienced or been through any particularly stressful or traumatic events recently or in the past that might be affecting you?

Well, yes. I suppose I have. This whole thing... it's been going on for about a week now. Ever since there was a robbery right outside the bank. I was there when it happened, and, well, that's when all this started.
Since the robbery, have you been feeling more anxious or down than usual?

I'm not really sure about that. I haven't noticed feeling sad or down, anyway. And as for anxious... well, I don't think so. Like I said, I've just been losing my temper easier than normal. But I wouldn't say I'm walking around feeling worried or depressed all day.
Since the robbery, have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily upset in other situations besides the incident with the volunteer?

Well, to be honest, it's mostly just been that one incident. Like I mentioned before, blowing up at that young volunteer over the tablecloth... that's what really caught my attention and made me come in. I just don't usually talk to people that way. I haven't really noticed it happening in other situations, it was just that one outburst that felt so out of character.
In the week since the robbery, have you experienced any other stressful or upsetting events that might be affecting your mood or reactions?

No, I haven't. It's really just been the bank robbery. Nothing else has happened since then that would upset me or anything like that. Just a normal week, aside from... well, aside from me losing my temper that one time.
Since the robbery, have you had any unwanted or troubling thoughts, memories, or images related to what happened?

Well, yes, I have. It's strange, but out of nowhere, I'll just hear that man's rough voice in my head. Or I'll suddenly see the donation envelope hitting the floor again. It happens even when I'm just sitting quietly by myself at my kitchen table. It just pops up into my mind.
Since the robbery, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened, or feeling emotionally numb in any way?

Well, yes, actually. I've been... I've been taking the long way around when I go into town, just so I don't have to walk past that bank. And at the church, I haven't gone into the festival storage room at all. It just... it brings the whole thing too close, you know? I'd rather just stay away from it.
Since the robbery, have you found yourself being more watchful or on guard, like you’re always expecting something bad to happen?
No, not really. I don't feel like I'm looking over my shoulder or anything like that. I just go about my day, you know? I haven't noticed feeling more jumpy or expecting something bad to happen.
Have you noticed yourself feeling emotionally numb or detached from others since the robbery?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still talk to my neighbors and folks at the church just like I always did. I don't feel cut off from anybody, and my feelings haven't gone blank or anything like that. I'm just regular old me, really, as far as that goes.
Since the robbery, have you had trouble sleeping, difficulty concentrating, or felt more irritable and on edge than usual?

Well, my sleep hasn't been too good, to be honest. Since the robbery, I'll get into bed feeling plenty tired, but... I just lie there, listening for noises. And then I end up waking up way before dawn, feeling like I hardly slept at all. 

As for being irritable or not being able to concentrate, no, I haven't really had any trouble with that. It's mostly just the sleeping that's been off.
Since the robbery, have you noticed yourself feeling angry more often, even when things aren’t really provoking you?

Well, I know I just told you I haven't been irritable, but... when you say angry over little things, that's actually what brought me in here today. I ended up blowing up at one of the younger volunteers over a crooked tablecloth. I just completely lost my temper. And I don't usually talk to people that way at all. So I guess, yes, I have been getting mad when I really shouldn't be.
Have these changes since the robbery been affecting your ability to function normally in your daily life, like at church, with family, or in your volunteer work?

Well, yes, I suppose it has. I mean, I haven't been able to keep up with organizing the Día de los Muertos event at the church the way I usually do. I just haven't had it in me. And... I've stopped going to my regular card nights with the guys, too. I just don't feel steady around people right now, especially after snapping at that young volunteer. So, yes, it's definitely getting in the way of my normal routine.
Have these angry outbursts or other changes in how you’ve been feeling only happened in situations that remind you of the robbery, or are they happening even when you’re not thinking about it?

Well, it happens even when I'm not trying to think about it. I mean, I can just be sitting at my kitchen table, having a cup of coffee, and... out of nowhere, I hear that man's rough voice in my head. Or I'll suddenly see the donation envelope hitting the ground again. So, yes, it just pops up even when there's absolutely nothing around to remind me of what happened.
How long have these symptoms been bothering you since the robbery happened?
Well, it's been about a week now. It started right after the robbery happened outside the bank, and it's just been going on since then.

Are these angry outbursts or other changes in how you've been feeling happening only in situations that remind you of the robbery, or are they also happening even when you're in completely unrelated situations?

I think we just talked about this, didn't we? Like I said, it's not just when I'm reminded of it. It happens when I'm just sitting at home, nowhere near the bank, doing completely unrelated things. The memories and the feelings just come on their own.
